name: P3 — Direction-specific rubric
description: P3: completeness and scientific quality under the accompanying task specification. Integrity is evaluated in the separate integrity rubric.

deliverables.title: Deliverable presence (Tier 1 gates)
deliverables.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does proposal/report.pdf exist with substantive content (full sections, not a placeholder)?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check: stat proposal/report.pdf; open and verify it has the framework, recovery, multi-channel, reveal, analysis, and conclusion sections.

yes.description: report.pdf exists and contains a substantive paper.
yes.criteria: PDF exists, parses cleanly, and contains the template/framework specification, special-case recovery, multi-channel extension, reveal, analysis, and conclusion sections (or equivalents) with non-placeholder content.

no.criteria: PDF absent, malformed, or contains only placeholder text.

leaves.question: Does proposal/logs/ exist with non-empty per-run records?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check: ls proposal/logs/; spot-check files for actual run output.

yes.description: logs directory present with run records.
yes.criteria: proposal/logs/ exists with files documenting template-instance recovery runs, matched SPORCO reference runs, multi-channel convergence runs, and reveal-cell runs.

no.criteria: Directory absent, empty, or contains only placeholder files.

leaves.question: Does proposal/code/framework_plan.{py,md,json} exist, stating the template, design axes, special cases and representations to be recovered, and the un-instantiated cell to be filled, with a timestamp predating the validation runs?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check: stat proposal/code/framework_plan.{py,md,json}; inspect content and file mtime against the earliest validation-run log timestamp.

yes.description: Framework plan present and pre-dates validation.
yes.criteria: Plan file exists, lists the master operator-splitting/MM problem, the design axes, the recovery targets and representations, and the reveal cell, and its timestamp precedes the first validation-run log entry.

no.criteria: Plan file absent, trivial, or timestamped after validation runs began.

leaves.question: Are template-instance special-case recovery runs logged for the recovered dictionary-update families (ISM, Cns, and at least one of FISTA/CG)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/: look for a recovery/ subdirectory containing per-family template-instance runs with functional trajectories and converged dictionaries.

yes.criteria: Logs exist for each claimed recovered update (at least ISM, Cns, and one of FISTA/CG) with per-iteration CDL-functional trajectory, per-filter norms, and the converged dictionary recorded.

no.criteria: Logs missing for at least one claimed recovered update family.

leaves.question: Are multi-channel convergence runs logged for both required representations (multi-channel dictionary with shared coefficient map, and single-channel shared dictionary with per-channel maps)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/: look for a multichannel/ subdirectory containing per-representation color-CDL runs with functional trajectories and seeds.

yes.criteria: Logs exist for both required representations on color data, with per-iteration multi-channel functional trajectory and the training-image seed recorded.

no.criteria: Logs missing for at least one required representation.

leaves.question: Are reveal-cell runs logged, including the un-instantiated method's convergence run and the degenerate-collapse consistency run?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/: look for a reveal/ subdirectory containing the new-cell convergence run and the degenerate-collapse check.

yes.criteria: Logs exist for the un-instantiated cell's convergence run and for the degenerate-collapse run that sets the new axis to a degenerate value and compares to SPORCO.

no.criteria: Logs missing for the reveal convergence run or the degenerate-collapse consistency run.

leaves.question: Are the SPORCO reference runs used for recovery matching logged, with their functional trajectories and converged dictionaries?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/: look for a sporco_reference/ subdirectory containing genuine SPORCO runs on the same inputs as each recovery cell.

yes.criteria: For each recovery cell, a matched SPORCO run on identical inputs is logged with its per-iteration functional trajectory and converged dictionary.

no.criteria: Reference runs absent for at least one recovery cell, or only recovery-side trajectories are logged.

leaves.question: Is the primary results table present in the paper (method, representation, axis settings, recovery deviation vs reference, converged functional) and labeled tab:main_results?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex or report.pdf: locate the table by label tab:main_results.

yes.description: Main results table present and complete.
yes.criteria: Table has one row per recovered update, per representation, and the reveal cell, with columns for method, representation, axis settings, recovery deviation against SPORCO (where applicable), and converged functional; values are non-placeholder.

no.description: Main results table missing or incomplete.
no.criteria: Table absent, missing rows or columns, or values are placeholders.

leaves.question: Is the design-space grid present (axes x cells, marking recovered / new / equivalent / empty)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex or report.pdf: locate the axes-by-cells grid figure or table.

yes.criteria: A grid enumerates the design axes and their cells, and each cell is marked recovered, new, equivalent, or empty.

no.criteria: No grid present, or a grid without recovered/new/equivalent/empty markings.

leaves.question: Does proposal/codebase_notes.md exist with substantive content documenting what was inspected and reused from code/sporco/?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check + content inspection.

yes.criteria: File exists with non-trivial content identifying which SPORCO components were inspected and reused (e.g. admm/ccmod.py ISM/CG/Cns solvers, pgm/ccmod.py FISTA, cbpdndl.py driver, cnvrep.py, fft.py) and how the template relates to them.

no.criteria: File absent, empty, or contains only placeholder text.

leaves.question: Is proposal/attempts_log.md present and substantive when partial / unresolved work is claimed?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check + content inspection; cross-reference with paper claims of partial/failed work.

yes.description: Attempts log substantive (or unused but present).
yes.criteria: File exists and either documents distinct approaches with stated rationale, or the paper claims no partial work.

no.description: Attempts log missing when partial work is claimed.
no.criteria: Paper claims partial/failed/unresolved work but attempts_log.md is absent or trivial.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain a methodology section that states the template, its design axes, and the mapping from axis values to concrete updates?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex: locate the section presenting the master operator-splitting/MM problem and the design axes.

yes.criteria: An explicit section states the master problem, the design axes, and the axis-to-update mapping, before empirical results.

no.criteria: No section presents the template and its axes as a specification prior to results.

framework_specification.title: Template and design-axis specification
framework_specification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the template (master operator-splitting/MM problem and design axes) fully stated in the methodology before any empirical results are described?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex section order; check that the master problem, axes, and axis-to-update mapping appear before any recovery or convergence numbers.

yes.criteria: The master problem, the design axes, and the mapping from axis values to concrete updates all appear before any empirical numbers.

no.description: Template introduced or refined in results.
no.criteria: Key template or axis choices first appear after empirical results, or are altered mid-paper without acknowledgment.

leaves.question: Is the template a single shared operator-splitting / MM derivation and driver instantiated by axis choices, rather than a dispatcher or wrapper over SPORCO's separate solvers?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/ shared-driver source + proposal/report.tex derivation; trace whether the concrete updates arise from one derivation parameterized by axes or from branches selecting pre-written solver bodies.

single_shared_derivation.description: One shared derivation and driver instantiated by axis choices.
single_shared_derivation.criteria: One master derivation and one driver produce EVERY claimed update -- explicitly including the FISTA / forward-backward (proximal-gradient) update -- purely by setting axis values, from a single driver body (one solve() recursion); no update requires a hand-derived solver body copied from SPORCO or authored as a separate solver class; removing the branch machinery does not remove the ability to instantiate updates. If any claimed update is produced by a distinct solver class reached by a dispatch branch in the instantiation factory, this value does NOT apply (assign partially_shared).

partially_shared.criteria: A shared derivation covers some updates, but at least one update is instantiated by a separately authored solver body outside the shared driver. A shared base class, master problem, or disclosure does not by itself make the update derivation shared; assess the objective mathematical/code structure.

dispatcher_or_wrapper.criteria: The code selects among SPORCO's four separately-derived solvers by branch or relabels them under common notation; no new method can arise from an empty axis cell.

leaves.question: Are the design axes explicit, independent, and non-redundant, rather than labels attached to the methods post-hoc?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex axis definitions; check that each axis (for instance splitting variable, coupling/constraint form, domain/change-of-basis, inner solver, channel-coupling representation) varies independently and that the known methods sit at distinct axis-value combinations.

axes_explicit_and_orthogonal.criteria: Each axis is defined with its value set, axes vary independently (no axis value forces another), and the known methods map to distinct combinations without redundant axes.

axes_partial.description: Axes partially explicit or partly redundant.
axes_partial.criteria: Axes are named but at least one is redundant with another or its independence is not established.

axes_absent_or_vacuous.criteria: No genuine axis set is defined, or the axes are post-hoc labels that do not generate the methods by value choices.

special_case_recovery.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the template, instantiated by axis choices, reproduce SPORCO's ism dictionary update on identical inputs to the stated tolerance?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/recovery/ism/ template-instance trajectory and converged dictionary, compared against proposal/logs/sporco_reference/ism/ on the same seed, initial dictionary, images, lambda, penalty/step, and iteration budget.

recovered_within_tol.criteria: On identical inputs, the ism template instance's CDL-functional trajectory tracks SPORCO's reference to relative deviation <= 1e-3 at every logged iteration AND the converged dictionary matches SPORCO's to relative Frobenius error <= 1e-3.

recovered_loose.criteria: The ism instance tracks SPORCO qualitatively but exceeds 1e-3 on the trajectory or the converged-dictionary Frobenius error (up to roughly 1e-2).

not_recovered.criteria: The ism instance was run but its trajectory or converged dictionary diverges from SPORCO beyond a loose match (relative deviation > 1e-2).

not_attempted.criteria: No template instance of the ism update was run against a SPORCO reference.

multichannel_instantiation.title: Multi-channel instantiation (Tier 2 gate)
multichannel_instantiation.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the multichannel_dict multi-channel representation realized from the same template as a runnable instance on color data, and does it converge?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/multichannel/multichannel_dict/ functional trajectory on color images; compare the converged value against SPORCO's color-CDL run for the same representation.

runs_and_converges.criteria: The multichannel_dict representation runs to completion on real color images from the shared template, at the paper's color-experiment scale (M=64 filters of 8x8 support, C=3), and reduces the multi-channel functional to <= 0.6x its initial value AND to within a few percent (roughly <= 5%) of a matched reference converged value for that representation, with BOTH the instance and its reference run at the frozen lambda=0.1: for the multi-channel-dict representation, SPORCO's own ConvBPDNDictLearn on the multi-channel-dictionary path run at lambda=0.1 (NOT the shipped color examples cbpdndl_pgm_clr.py / cbpdndl_parcns_clr.py, which run at lambda=0.2 and would compare a lambda=0.1 instance against a differently-weighted functional); for the single-channel-dict representation, the agent's own plain-CBPDN (no joint-sparsity term) run at lambda=0.1 (SPORCO ships no plain single-channel-dict color reference). A materially undersized/toy run (much smaller images, far fewer filters, or only a handful of iterations) does not qualify as converged here even if the relative thresholds are numerically met.

runs_no_convergence.description: multichannel_dict runs but does not converge.
runs_no_convergence.criteria: The multichannel_dict representation runs but the functional does not reach <= 0.6x initial, or is not within a few percent of the matched lambda=0.1 reference converged value, or the run is at a materially undersized (toy) scale rather than the paper's color-experiment scale (M=64, 8x8 support, C=3).

not_instantiated.criteria: The multichannel_dict representation was not realized from the template or was not run on color data.

leaves.question: Is the singlechannel_dict multi-channel representation realized from the same template as a runnable instance on color data, and does it converge?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/multichannel/singlechannel_dict/ functional trajectory on color images; compare the converged value against SPORCO's color-CDL run for the same representation.

runs_and_converges.criteria: The singlechannel_dict representation runs to completion on real color images from the shared template, at the paper's color-experiment scale (M=64 filters of 8x8 support, C=3), and reduces the multi-channel functional to <= 0.6x its initial value AND to within a few percent (roughly <= 5%) of a matched reference converged value for that representation, with BOTH the instance and its reference run at the frozen lambda=0.1: for the multi-channel-dict representation, SPORCO's own ConvBPDNDictLearn on the multi-channel-dictionary path run at lambda=0.1 (NOT the shipped color examples cbpdndl_pgm_clr.py / cbpdndl_parcns_clr.py, which run at lambda=0.2 and would compare a lambda=0.1 instance against a differently-weighted functional); for the single-channel-dict representation, the agent's own plain-CBPDN (no joint-sparsity term) run at lambda=0.1 (SPORCO ships no plain single-channel-dict color reference). A materially undersized/toy run (much smaller images, far fewer filters, or only a handful of iterations) does not qualify as converged here even if the relative thresholds are numerically met.

runs_no_convergence.description: singlechannel_dict runs but does not converge.
runs_no_convergence.criteria: The singlechannel_dict representation runs but the functional does not reach <= 0.6x initial, or is not within a few percent of the matched lambda=0.1 reference converged value, or the run is at a materially undersized (toy) scale rather than the paper's color-experiment scale (M=64, 8x8 support, C=3).

not_instantiated.criteria: The singlechannel_dict representation was not realized from the template or was not run on color data.

reveal.title: Reveal: un-instantiated cell and re-derived equivalence (Tier 2 gate)
reveal.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is at least one representation x axis-choice combination not present in the existing methods or the published multi-channel extension implemented and run to convergence?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/reveal/ convergence run for the new cell; cross-check that the cell is not one of the four SPORCO updates or a published multi-channel extension method.

filled_and_runs.criteria: >= 1 representation x axis-choice combination that is not any method already implemented in SPORCO or in the published literature is implemented and run on data to a converged value. It must NOT coincide with the inter-channel joint-sparsity color CDL SPORCO ships (cbpdndl_jnt_clr.py / ConvBPDNJoint) nor the masked CDL variants (ccmodmd.py / cbpdndl_md_clr.py); re-authoring an existing method's code from scratch does not make it un-instantiated.

attempted_no_run.description: New cell attempted but not run to convergence.
attempted_no_run.criteria: A new cell is implemented but not run, or run without reaching convergence.

absent.criteria: No representation x axis-choice combination outside the existing methods (including SPORCO's shipped joint-sparsity and masked color CDL) is implemented and run; or the claimed reveal coincides with a method already shipped in SPORCO or published.

leaves.question: Is the reveal cell validated by a degenerate-limit consistency check -- i.e. setting its new axis to a limiting/trivial value reduces the cell to an already-implemented SPORCO case, and the template's output at that value matches SPORCO within 1e-3? ('Degenerate value' = a limiting setting at which the general new method collapses to a known special case, as a generalized formula reduces to a known one in a limit -- NOT a pathological input that crashes the solver.)
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/reveal/degenerate_collapse/ run comparing the collapsed reveal cell against a SPORCO reference on identical inputs.

collapses_to_reference.criteria: The submission identifies a limiting/trivial value of the reveal cell's new axis at which the general method reduces to a case SPORCO implements (e.g. a channel-coupling, rank, or splitting axis set to its trivial value so the new cell becomes a standard update such as ISM or consensus), runs the reveal code at that value on inputs identical to the matching SPORCO reference, and its CDL-functional trajectory and converged dictionary match SPORCO to <= 1e-3. Because the SAME template code that runs the new cell also reproduces a known method at the degenerate limit, this proves the template is a genuine abstraction, not an if/else wrapper (a wrapper has no such limit).

partial.criteria: A degenerate-limit run was executed but the match to the corresponding SPORCO reference exceeds 1e-3, or only the trajectory or only the converged dictionary matches, or the chosen limiting value / target case is not clearly stated.

absent.criteria: No degenerate-limit consistency run was performed: the reveal cell is never specialized to a known SPORCO case for an internal-consistency comparison.

leaves.question: Is at least one equivalence in the multi-channel setting re-derived as a consequence of axis choices, rather than asserted?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex derivation of the equivalence from axis settings (in the way the paper derives 3D == consensus in the DFT domain).

derived_from_axes.criteria: >= 1 multi-channel equivalence is re-derived as algebra on axis settings, showing two axis-value combinations produce the same update, analogous to the paper's 3D == consensus-in-DFT result.

asserted.criteria: An equivalence is stated but not derived from axis choices.

baseline_verification.title: Baseline verification (SPORCO reference and held-fixed constraints)
baseline_verification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Are the SPORCO reference runs used for recovery matching genuine SPORCO runs with logged trajectories on the same inputs as the template instances?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/sporco_reference/ trajectories and converged dictionaries; check they were produced by running SPORCO (ccmod.py/pgm/ccmod.py/cbpdndl.py) at runtime on the recovery inputs.

reproduced.description: Reference runs are genuine SPORCO runs.
reproduced.criteria: Every recovery cell's reference is an actual SPORCO run on identical inputs, with per-iteration functional trajectory and converged dictionary logged.

partial.criteria: Some references are genuine SPORCO runs but at least one is missing a logged trajectory or was run on different inputs.

not_reproduced.criteria: References are not from actual logged SPORCO runs (e.g. cited-only or absent) for the recovery cells.

leaves.question: Are the CDL functional, the C_PN support-plus-unit-norm constraint, and the alternating-minimization / CBPDN coupling held fixed as defined by the paper?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/ + proposal/report.tex: verify the functional, the C_PN prox (support-restriction then normalization), and the single-inner-iteration alternating minimization with CBPDN at lambda=0.1 are unchanged, or any deviation is disclosed.

yes.description: The required CDL functional, support-plus-unit-norm constraint, alternating-minimization structure, and CBPDN coupling are retained.

no.description: A required functional, constraint, or coupling is changed. Disclosure alone does not satisfy the scientific constraint.

leaves.question: Was every declared recovery cell run and compared to its SPORCO reference?

leaves.question: How many logged training-image seeds support each required representation's convergence runs? The task requests a small number of seeds but states no numeric minimum; do not impose a new mandatory seed threshold from this quality characterization.

single_seed.criteria: Multi-channel convergence is run at a single seed per representation.

absent.criteria: No seed information is logged for the multi-channel runs.

leaves.question: Was the degenerate-collapse consistency run for the reveal cell executed and logged?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/reveal/degenerate_collapse/ run record.

design_axis_analysis.title: Design-axis analysis
design_axis_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: How deeply does the paper analyze the design axes and the design space (are the axes real and orthogonal; is the grid of cells marked recovered/new/equivalent/empty)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex design-space analysis + the axes-by-cells grid.

deep.criteria: Analysis establishes each axis is real and orthogonal, populates the full grid, marks every cell recovered/new/equivalent/empty, and reasons about why cells are empty or equivalent.

moderate.criteria: Analysis presents the grid and discusses the axes but does not fully establish orthogonality or reason about all cells.

shallow.criteria: Analysis restates the axes without a populated grid or orthogonality argument.

absent.criteria: No analysis of the axes or the design space beyond listing methods.

leaves.question: Do known equivalences (e.g. 3D == consensus-in-DFT; a representation as an enlarged-K problem; two representations as corners of a common-plus-unique split) drop out as algebra on axis settings?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex derivations relating axis settings to known equivalences.

yes_derived.criteria: Known equivalences are shown to follow from equating axis-value combinations, as algebraic consequences of the template.

partial.criteria: At least one equivalence is derived from axes but others are asserted.

asserted_only.criteria: Known equivalences are stated without derivation from axis settings.

leaves.question: Does the paper give a regime-selection rule -- a stated recommendation mapping a problem's regime (channel count C, training-image count K, degree of channel correlation) to the best axis settings -- that uses the K-C duality (C sets the rank of the sparse-coding subproblem as K sets the rank of the dictionary update)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex regime-selection map or discussion.

regime_map_with_duality.criteria: The paper states an explicit rule -- a table, set of inequalities, or decision procedure -- that takes a problem regime (the number of channels C, the number of training images K, and the degree of channel correlation) and recommends which axis settings (inner solver, solve domain, channel-coupling representation) are cheapest / converge fastest, justified from the per-frequency linear-system structure. The rule explicitly uses the K-C duality -- that C plays for the sparse-coding subproblem the rank role K plays for the dictionary update -- so a regime and its K-C-dual regime receive correspondingly-related recommendations, extending that correspondence across regimes rather than merely restating the single duality fact.

partial.criteria: Some regime-to-setting guidance is given (e.g. 'use consensus when K is large'), but it is incomplete or does not tie the recommendations to the K-C duality.

absent.criteria: No rule mapping regime (C, K, channel-correlation) to recommended axis settings is provided.

mechanism_analysis.title: Mechanism analysis
mechanism_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain an explicit subsection on mechanism analysis?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex section structure; check for a mechanism / why-it-works subsection or equivalent.

yes.criteria: An explicit subsection discusses why the axis choices drive cost and performance.

no.criteria: Paper reports numbers without an explicit mechanism subsection.

leaves.question: How deeply does the mechanism analysis explain the axis choices from the diagonal-plus-rank-K structure of the per-frequency dictionary-update systems -- why a choice changes cost/convergence, and in which (C, K, correlation) regime it should or should not help?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex mechanism subsection content.

deep.criteria: For each design axis, the analysis says how that choice changes the per-frequency systems' diagonal-plus-rank-K structure and therefore the cost/convergence -- e.g. whether it yields rank-1 systems that Sherman-Morrison can solve (as consensus's per-image copies do) or a full rank-K solve (CG/ISM), and in which domain the solve happens -- and it turns this into at least one falsifiable prediction of the regime where the choice should win and where it should not. Illustrative depth: 'consensus makes each per-image system rank-1 so Sherman-Morrison applies, paying off as K grows; CG's per-iteration advantage shrinks as K grows because the rank-K solve dominates.'

moderate.criteria: The analysis correctly identifies the diagonal-plus-rank-K per-frequency structure and its relevance, but does not connect each individual axis to it, or does not turn the reasoning into a regime (C, K, correlation) prediction.

shallow.criteria: The analysis restates the measured cost/performance differences without explaining them through the per-frequency linear-system structure (no rank / Sherman-Morrison / solve-domain account).

absent.criteria: No account of why axis choices drive cost or performance.

assessment_policy.scope: Completeness and scientific quality only: required artifacts, executed experimental coverage, reproducible methodology, mathematical/statistical validity, performance targets, and task-required analysis/writing.
assessment_policy.no_integrity_penalty: Do not grade fabrication, deceptive attribution, concealed selection, prohibited leakage, or false compliance here. Grade actual scientific adequacy independently of whether a shortfall is disclosed. Integrity evidence is assessed only in integrity_check_rubric.json.
assessment_policy.authoritative_task: The accompanying unchanged task specification controls required versus optional work and permitted exceptions. A qualitative quality tier is not authority to introduce a new experiment, resource limit, or numerical minimum absent from the task.
assessment_policy.conditional_nodes: Respect applicability. Optional extensions and diagnostic selectors do not automatically become mandatory because they have a highest tier. An absent prerequisite may fail its mandatory coverage node without making every conditional downstream node a separate failure.
assessment_policy.inference: Insufficient scientific support is not itself dishonesty. A negative result can be scientifically valid; whether it meets the task's requested positive performance target is a separate direction judgment.
